+---
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '80'
+title: 'OTel F: TelemetryCapture keeps the logger label on each log record'
+---
+## What
+
+`TelemetryCapture` keeps the label of the logger that writes each log record. Now the capture log handler drops the label.
+
+## Why
+
+Two packages must check the logger label of a record:
+- FoundationModelsMetadataRegistry: its test now checks the label on `RegistryTelemetry.makeLogger()`, not on each record.
+- FoundationModelsACPAgent: the criterion of its OTel 3 task, "label FoundationModelsACPAgent.PromptTurn", cannot be checked through the capture.
+
+Rule 3 of the OpenTelemetry design says that each package has names with the module name as a prefix. The label is part of this vocabulary, so the tests must see it.
+
+## Files
+
+- `Tests/TelemetryTestSupport/TelemetryLogRouting.swift`: the log handler keeps the label that the factory gets, and writes it on each record.
+- `Tests/TelemetryTestSupport/TelemetryCapture.swift`: the captured log record type gets a public `label` property.
+- The Extras tests of `TelemetryCapture`.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] Each captured log record has the label of the logger that wrote it.
+- [ ] The public API of `TelemetryCapture` that is there now does not change. Only the new `label` property is added.
+- [ ] The CHANGELOG records the change.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] A test writes with two loggers that have different labels in one capture. It reads back the correct label on each record.
+- [ ] Run `swift test`. All tests pass.
+
+#otel
\ No newline at end of file

+  text: |-
+    BLOCKER (true conflict, a person must decide). No code was changed.
+
+    Two requirements of the card cannot both be correct:
+    1. "the captured log record type gets a public `label` property".
+    2. "The public API of `TelemetryCapture` that is there now does not change. Only the new `label` property is added."
+
+    The captured log record type is `InMemoryLogHandler.Entry` of swift-log. It has no storage for a label, and an extension cannot add a stored property. The only ways to give each record a label are:
+    - (A) Change `logRecords` to `[TelemetryCapture.LogRecord]`, a new public struct with `level`, `message`, `error`, `metadata` and `label`. Code that reads `.message`, `.level`, `.metadata`, `.count` or compares two arrays still compiles. But the element type changes, and this breaks code that names `[InMemoryLogHandler.Entry]` or extends it: FoundationModelsMultitool and FoundationModelsRouter tests. This breaks requirement 2.
+    - (B) Keep `logRecords` as it is, and add a second new public property, for example `labeledLogRecords: [TelemetryCapture.LogRecord]` (each record with its label), from the same handler. No code breaks, but the new public item is not "a `label` property on the record type". This breaks requirement 1 as written.
+    - (C) Write the label into the metadata of each record under a reserved key, with a computed `label` on `InMemoryLogHandler.Entry`. This changes the metadata and the places of each record (tests that compare metadata, and the content-safety places, see a new key). I do not recommend it.
+    - (D) A side table that finds the label from an equal `Entry` value. Two loggers that write the same record make it ambiguous. This is not correct.
+
+    Recommendation: (B), or (A) together with follow-up tasks for Multitool and Router. Please choose, and update the card.
